en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Isa Bin Suleyman Al Nahhas, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, from Al Khaybari and Yunus Bin Zabyan both said,

‘We both heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from the things more beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> than the extraction of the Dirhams to (give to) the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Make for him in the Paradise a mountain like Ohad, due to his making the Dirham to him<sup>asws</sup>.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted is Saying in His<sup>azwj</sup> Book
[2:245] Who is it that who will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He will Multiply it to him manifold?
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! It is regarding helping the Imam<sup>asws</sup> in particular’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people has narrated Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Isa ibn Sulayman al-Nahhas from al-Mufaddl ibn ‘Umar from al-Khaybari and Yunus ibn Zabyan who both have said we heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say the following.
“There is nothing more beloved to Allah than the Dirhams taken out (of one’s property) to pay to the Imam (a.s.). On the Day of Judgment Allah will his Dirham as big as the mountain of ’Uhud.”
“Allah, the Most High has said in His book, “One who generously lends to God will be paid back in many multiples of the loan. . .” [2:245]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “This is a special reference to the payment made to the Imam.”
